problem:
Suppose ${\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s=4$ for some function $f(x,y),$ where ${C}_{1}$ is parametrized by ${r}_{1}(t)=⟨{t}^{4}-3{t}^{2},\,t⟩$ for $0\le t\le 2.$

Which of the following must be true?

- ${\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s=-4$
- ${\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s=8,$ where ${C}_{2}$ is parametrized by ${r}_{2}(u)=⟨16{u}^{4}-12{u}^{2},\,2u⟩$ for $0\le u\le 1.$
- ${\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s=4$

activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Line Integrals of Scalar Functions
